text.hi: It is named after a man who never saw it. Sir George Everest, a former Surveyor General of India, even objected to the honour, but the name became official in 1865. He pronounced it 'Eve-rest'.
text.en: It is named after a man who never saw it. Sir George Everest, a former Surveyor General of India, even objected to the honour, but the name became official in 1865. He pronounced it 'Eve-rest'.

text.hi: An Indian mathematician found it first: in 1852 Radhanath Sikdar, working for the survey at Dehradun, calculated that Peak XV was the highest mountain in the world.
text.en: An Indian mathematician found it first: in 1852 Radhanath Sikdar, working for the survey at Dehradun, calculated that Peak XV was the highest mountain in the world.

text.hi: The 1856 survey worked out exactly 29,000 ft, but that looked too much like a rounded guess, so the announced height was 29,002 ft.
text.en: The 1856 survey worked out exactly 29,000 ft, but that looked too much like a rounded guess, so the announced height was 29,002 ft.

text.hi: The very top is made of limestone that formed on an ancient sea floor, with marine fossils. The IUGS listed these 'highest rocks on the planet' as a geological heritage site in 2022.
text.en: The very top is made of limestone that formed on an ancient sea floor, with marine fossils. The IUGS listed these 'highest rocks on the planet' as a geological heritage site in 2022.

text.hi: Everest is still growing. GPS shows it rising about 2 mm a year, and a 2024 study says a river capture about 89,000 years ago has lifted it 15–50 m higher than it would otherwise be.
text.en: Everest is still growing. GPS shows it rising about 2 mm a year, and a 2024 study says a river capture about 89,000 years ago has lifted it 15–50 m higher than it would otherwise be.

text.hi: Its height grew by 86 cm on paper in 2020, when Nepal and China agreed for the first time to measure the snow cap, not just the rock.
text.en: Its height grew by 86 cm on paper in 2020, when Nepal and China agreed for the first time to measure the snow cap, not just the rock.

text.hi: It is the highest point above sea level, but not the tallest mountain: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from its base on the ocean floor, and Ecuador's Chimborazo summit is farther from Earth's centre because Earth bulges at the equator.
text.en: It is the highest point above sea level, but not the tallest mountain: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from its base on the ocean floor, and Ecuador's Chimborazo summit is farther from Earth's centre because Earth bulges at the equator.

text.hi: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the top at 11:30 am on 29 May 1953. Years later Tenzing revealed that Hillary had stepped on the summit first.
text.en: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the top at 11:30 am on 29 May 1953. Years later Tenzing revealed that Hillary had stepped on the summit first.

text.hi: Before Everest, Edmund Hillary was a beekeeper in New Zealand, working with his father and brother.
text.en: Before Everest, Edmund Hillary was a beekeeper in New Zealand, working with his father and brother.

text.hi: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to summit, at 1:07 pm on 23 May 1984, after surviving an avalanche that hit her camp a week earlier.
text.en: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to summit, at 1:07 pm on 23 May 1984, after surviving an avalanche that hit her camp a week earlier.

text.hi: Arunima Sinha lost a leg in 2011 after robbers pushed her from a train. On 21 May 2013 she became, as widely reported, the first female amputee to climb Everest.
text.en: Arunima Sinha lost a leg in 2011 after robbers pushed her from a train. On 21 May 2013 she became, as widely reported, the first female amputee to climb Everest.

text.hi: Malavath Purna from Telangana reached the top from the Tibet side on 25 May 2014, aged 13 years and 11 months, making her the youngest girl ever to summit.
text.en: Malavath Purna from Telangana reached the top from the Tibet side on 25 May 2014, aged 13 years and 11 months, making her the youngest girl ever to summit.

text.hi: Kami Rita Sherpa, 'Everest Man', has stood on top 32 times, the latest on 17 May 2026 at age 56. His first summit was in 1994.
text.en: Kami Rita Sherpa, 'Everest Man', has stood on top 32 times, the latest on 17 May 2026 at age 56. His first summit was in 1994.

text.hi: Lhakpa Sherpa holds the women's record with 11 summits, reached on the same day in May 2026 that Kami Rita made his 32nd.
text.en: Lhakpa Sherpa holds the women's record with 11 summits, reached on the same day in May 2026 that Kami Rita made his 32nd.

text.hi: The youngest summiter is Jordan Romero (USA), aged 13 in 2010. The oldest is Yuichiro Miura (Japan), aged 80 years and 223 days in 2013.
text.en: The youngest summiter is Jordan Romero (USA), aged 13 in 2010. The oldest is Yuichiro Miura (Japan), aged 80 years and 223 days in 2013.

text.hi: Spring 2026 was the busiest season ever, with 1,008 summits from the Nepal side and 274 people on top on a single day (20 May).
text.en: Spring 2026 was the busiest season ever, with 1,008 summits from the Nepal side and 274 people on top on a single day (20 May).

text.hi: Sherpas and other hired climbers now make more summits than paying clients: 7,081 vs 6,656 up to the end of 2025.
text.en: Sherpas and other hired climbers now make more summits than paying clients: 7,081 vs 6,656 up to the end of 2025.

text.hi: At the summit the air pressure is only about a third of sea level. A person flown straight there from sea level, above 8,500 m, would likely pass out within two or three minutes.
text.en: At the summit the air pressure is only about a third of sea level. A person flown straight there from sea level, above 8,500 m, would likely pass out within two or three minutes.

text.hi: A Nepali permit to climb the normal route in spring costs US$15,000 per person since September 2025, up from US$11,000.
text.en: A Nepali permit to climb the normal route in spring costs US$15,000 per person since September 2025, up from US$11,000.

text.hi: The summit has been described as about the size of a dining-room table.
text.en: The summit has been described as about the size of a dining-room table.

summary.hi: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It sits in the Mahalangur Himal section of the Himalayas, and the Nepal–China border runs across its summit. Nepal and China jointly announced its current official height, 8,848.86 m, on 8 December 2020. Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary made the first confirmed ascent on 29 May 1953, and by the end of 2025 the Himalayan Database counted 13,737 summits by 7,563 different people.
summary.en: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It sits in the Mahalangur Himal section of the Himalayas, and the Nepal–China border runs across its summit. Nepal and China jointly announced its current official height, 8,848.86 m, on 8 December 2020. Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary made the first confirmed ascent on 29 May 1953, and by the end of 2025 the Himalayan Database counted 13,737 summits by 7,563 different people.
